definition: A defense that pushes air troops back in the direction it faces. It deals no damage, so its facing decides which side of the base is slow for air attacks.
example: Both sweepers face the Town Hall side, so the Lava Hounds go in from the back.

definition: A layout built to deny the second star, usually by keeping the Town Hall deep and hard to reach so attacks stop at one star.
example: An anti-2 star base is a strong pick for Clan War Leagues where every star counts.

definition: A layout built to prevent a full three-star attack, often giving up the Town Hall while spreading defenses to slow the army down.
example: Most war bases at the top are anti-3 star; the two-star is accepted.

definition: The share URL the game produces for a troop, spell and siege machine composition. Opening it fills the army slots without typing anything.
example: Tap the army link on a strategy page to load the army in the game.

definition: The share URL the game produces for a layout. Opening it copies the layout into a free base slot on an account at that Town Hall or one level higher.
example: A base link for Town Hall 14 opens on a Town Hall 14 or 15 account.

definition: A Dark spell that spawns bats over time. Bats target defenses and are countered by splash damage, so attackers drop them after key splash defenses fall.
example: Freeze the Wizard Towers before the bat spells land.

definition: A siege machine that tunnels under walls to a target, surfacing to deliver the clan castle troops close to the core.
The first Builder Base hero, repaired at Builder Hall 5. A melee unit with a hammer that gains an ability at level 5.
The building, unlocked at Town Hall 8, where hero equipment is unlocked and upgraded with ores. Upgrades finish instantly.
example: Spend ores at the Blacksmith on the equipment you actually attack with.

definition: The Battle Blimp, a flying siege machine that carries clan castle troops over walls and drops them where it is destroyed or where its target stands.
example: The blimp carried Super Archers straight to the Town Hall.

definition: The second village, reached by boat, with its own buildings, troops and battles. Progress there is separate from the home village.
The central building of the Builder Base. At level 6 a second stage opens with O.T.T.O's Outpost as its centre.
example: Upgrading the Builder Hall unlocks the second stage of the base.

definition: Short for Clan Castle. It holds donated troops, spells and a siege machine, on offense and on defense.
example: Lure the CC before the main army walks in.

definition: A clan-versus-clan battle with a preparation day and a war day. Each member attacks a base on the other side and the clan with more stars wins.
Troops held back to finish the outside buildings after the main army has gone through, so the attack still reaches the percentage it needs.
example: Save a few Archers and a Hog Rider for clean-up on the far corner.

definition: A Builder Base building that speeds up time in that village while active. It has no defensive role.
A spell that creates temporary copies of troops inside its radius, up to a housing limit. The copies vanish when the spell runs out.
example: Drop the clone on the Electro Dragons after they pass the first ring.

definition: A cheap attack aimed only at the mines, collectors and drills on the outside of a base, skipping the storages.
One enclosed section of a base surrounded by walls. More compartments mean more wall breaks before troops reach the core.
example: The Town Hall sits in a small compartment with no direct path in.

definition: The central section of a base where the Town Hall or the most important defenses sit. Most attack plans aim to get there.
example: The Warden's aura should cover the army as it enters the core.

definition: Clan War Leagues. Groups of eight clans fight seven wars over eight days, one war against each rival, and each member gets one attack per war.
example: In CWL a missed attack cannot be made up, so plan the hit before the timer runs down.

definition: The third resource, used for heroes, Dark troops and Dark spells. It is scarce, so bases keep it near the core.
A base whose owner has not logged in for a while, so its collectors are full and easy loot for a collector raid.
example: Dead bases show full collectors and an overgrown look.

definition: Placing troops, heroes, spells or a siege machine on the battlefield. The order and spot of each deployment decide how the attack unfolds.
Dropping trophies on purpose to sit in a lower league, where bases are easier and loot is plentiful, at the cost of smaller league rewards.
A long-range defense that only activates once a set amount of troop housing has been deployed. It fires at the largest cluster of troops.
example: The queen walk stays below the Eagle Artillery's activation threshold.

definition: One of the two places a hero can carry equipment. The two pieces chosen together define the hero's ability in that attack.
example: The Queen runs Giant Arrow in one slot and Healer Puppet in the other.

definition: Grand Warden equipment. When the ability fires, every unit around the Warden, including himself, becomes invincible for its duration.
example: Pop the Eternal Tome as the Scattershot fires.

definition: A siege machine that stays outside the base and lobs fireballs at buildings from long range, releasing its clan castle troops when destroyed.
A spell that stops defenses and enemy troops in its radius for a few seconds. It unlocks at Town Hall 9 and its duration grows with each level.
example: Freeze the single Inferno Tower before it locks onto the hero.

definition: Troops or heroes placed on the flanks so the main army walks into the core instead of around the edge.
example: Two Baby Dragons on each side make a wide funnel for the Electro Dragons.

definition: The Town Hall weapon at Town Halls 13 to 16. It fires at troops near the Town Hall and leaves a damaging effect when the Town Hall is destroyed.
The Town Hall 12 weapon. It hits several targets at once and only appears once the Town Hall is damaged or the base is over half destroyed.
example: Send the tank in first so the Giga Tesla wakes up on something sturdy.

definition: Items that decide what a hero's ability does. Each hero carries two at a time; they are upgraded with ores at the Blacksmith.
A unit assigned to one hero from the Pet House, unlocked at Town Hall 14. Each pet has its own ability, and each hero carries one pet.
example: L.A.S.S.I is the first pet, ready as soon as the Pet House is built.

definition: The share of attacks that reach three stars with a given strategy. A high hit rate matters more than one spectacular hit.
example: Pick the army with the best hit rate for your Town Hall.

definition: The amount of damage a unit or building can take before it is destroyed. Often written HP.
An attack that mixes Hog Riders and Miners behind a hero charge, with Healers keeping the ground troops alive.
example: A queen charge into hybrid is a standard three-star plan for many Town Halls.

definition: The Town Hall 17 weapon, formed by merging the Town Hall with the Eagle Artillery. It fires fireballs that leave burning pools on impact.
A defense with two modes: single-target, which ramps up damage the longer it fires, or multi-target, which hits several units at lower damage.
example: A single-target Inferno melts a Golem, so freeze it or zap it.

definition: A spell, unlocked at Town Hall 11, that hides units inside its radius so nothing can target them until they leave it or the spell ends.
example: Invisibility on the blimp troops keeps the Town Hall weapon off them.

definition: A defense or building walled off on its own, away from the rest of the base, so an army has to break in again to reach it.
example: An Inferno Tower on an island behind the core stops a clean walk through.

definition: A spell that lets ground troops cross walls inside its radius for its duration, opening a path without breaking the wall.
example: Drop the jump on the wall between the two core compartments.

definition: A point where several wall segments meet. Wall breakers and the Wall Wrecker aim for junctions because one break there can open more than one compartment.
example: The Wall Wrecker breaks at the junction and opens both compartments.

definition: A small group, usually heroes plus a few troops, sent in first to take out a key part of the base such as the Town Hall or the clan castle troops.
example: The kill squad handles the Eagle Artillery before the main army lands.

definition: Lava Hounds and Balloons. The Hounds tank the Air Defenses while the Balloons destroy defenses behind them.
example: LaLo works best on bases with Air Defenses on one side.

definition: The top tier of Ranked Battles. Attacks and defenses are limited per day, opponents are assigned, and trophies reset at the end of the season.
example: In Legend League every attack counts, so warm up in Friendly Challenges.

definition: A siege machine, unlocked at Town Hall 13, that rolls logs through walls and buildings in a straight line towards the Town Hall.
example: Aim the Log Launcher so its logs cut a lane into the core.

definition: The gold, elixir and dark elixir an attacker takes from a base. The amount on offer shows before the attack starts.
The maximum resources one attack can take. Storages and collectors each give up only a share of what they hold, so a rich base is not fully drained.
A defense that deals damage based on a share of the target's maximum hitpoints, so it hurts tanky units and heroes most.
example: The Monolith is a priority target for the kill squad.

definition: Dropping troops along the whole edge of the base at once instead of in a plan. It rarely three-stars but can clear a weak base fast.
example: Nine-finger the Archers on a dead base and collect the loot.

definition: The resources used to upgrade hero equipment. They come mostly from wars, Ranked rewards, the Star Bonus and the trader rather than from raids.
example: Ores are the bottleneck for equipment, not gold.

definition: An Elixir spell, unlocked at Town Hall 12, that disables defenses and makes buildings in its radius invisible and invulnerable while it lasts.
example: Overgrowth on the outside Scattershots lets the army walk past them.

definition: The route troops take through a base, decided by their targeting rules and the layout. Reading pathing is what makes a funnel work.
example: The Hogs path around the compartment instead of through it.

definition: A Dark spell that damages and slows enemy troops in its area over time. Its main use is on clan castle troops and skeletons.
example: Poison the clan castle troops once they clump on the tank.

definition: The Earthquake spell, unlocked at Town Hall 8. It takes a share of hitpoints from buildings and walls; four of any level bring down any wall.
example: Four quakes open the core wall for the Hogs.

definition: A queen walk that pushes deeper into the base, usually with more Healers and a Rage, to take out key defenses or the Town Hall.
example: The queen charge cleared the Eagle Artillery before the hybrid went in.

definition: The Archer Queen walking the outside of a base with Healers behind her, clearing buildings and creating a funnel before the main army goes in.
example: Start the queen walk on the side with the Air Sweeper facing away.

definition: A spell that boosts the damage and speed of troops inside its radius while they stay in it.
example: Rage the Dragons as they hit the core.

definition: Ranked Battles, added in October 2025. Tournaments with a capped pool of attacks and a run of numbered leagues; trophies reset when each tournament ends.
example: Ranked replaced the old Bronze-to-Titan trophy ladder.

definition: A spell, unlocked at Town Hall 13, that returns troops, heroes and pets in its area to the deployment bar so they can be placed again.
example: Recall the queen after the walk and drop her with the main army.

definition: A layout with an outer ring of walls and buildings around the core, so ground troops circle the ring instead of walking in.
example: Ring bases punish attackers who skip the funnel.

definition: A siege machine, unlocked at Town Hall 13, that lands and spawns troops on the spot, then releases the clan castle troops when it is destroyed.
A vehicle built in the Workshop, unlocked at Town Hall 12, that carries the clan castle troops into a base. Each type takes a different route in.
example: A siege machine can also be donated by a clanmate.

definition: A Dark spell that summons skeletons in its radius. They set off traps, distract defenses and chip at a defense the army has not reached.
example: Two skeleton spells on the Scattershot keep it busy while the queen passes.

definition: A flying siege machine that drops boulders on defenses, dealing splash damage, and releases the clan castle troops when it is destroyed.
A building that holds gold, elixir or dark elixir. Storages give up a share of their contents when destroyed, so bases guard them in the core.
A high-hitpoint unit, such as a Golem or Lava Hound, placed first so defenses target it while damage dealers work behind it.
example: The Golem tanks the Inferno while the Wizards clear the compartment.

definition: The defense built into the Town Hall from level 12 upward: Giga Tesla, Giga Inferno, Inferno Artillery and later forms. It fires once the Town Hall is attacked.
A full-destruction attack: 100 percent of the base and all three stars. In war it is the result every attack aims for.
example: A three-star on the mirror keeps the clan ahead.

definition: The central building of the home village. Its level sets what can be built and which base links open: the same Town Hall or one level below.
example: A Town Hall 13 account cannot open a layout link made for Town Hall 14.

definition: Where the hidden traps sit in a layout. Good placement catches the common path of Hogs, Miners or Balloons rather than filling empty space.
example: Trap placement on the Hog route turned a three-star into a two.

definition: The newest siege machine, from Workshop level 8. It stays put and launches barrels of troops, including the clan castle troops, at your army to support it.
Attacking to climb leagues rather than for loot. The aim is stars and percentage on every hit, not resources.
example: Trophy pushing rewards a reliable army over a flashy one.

definition: The old name for Builder Base multiplayer attacks. Since Builder Base 2.0 there is no head-to-head: your own stars and percentage earn trophies, and defenses lose them.
The first siege machine, available once the Workshop is built at Town Hall 12. It drives through walls towards the Town Hall and drops troops when destroyed.
example: The Wall Wrecker takes the straight line to the core.

definition: The Grand Warden's active ability, unlocked with the hero at Town Hall 11. What it does depends on the equipment he carries.
example: Save the Warden ability for the Giga Inferno burst.

definition: The path troops take when the army goes around the base from one side to the other instead of through the middle.
example: The Hogs wrap around the back and never reach the core.

definition: The Lightning spell, the first spell available at Town Hall 5. It hits a small area and does no damage to the Town Hall, Clan Castle or storages.
example: Two zaps and a quake take out the Air Defense.

definition: Using Lightning spells plus one Earthquake to destroy a defense before the army reaches it. Common against Air Defenses and Infernos.
example: ZapQuake both Air Defenses on the far side before sending the Dragons.
